newsitem.title: USA: ABC/Money consumer comfort holds steady at 11.0.
newsitem.headline: ABC/Money consumer comfort holds steady at 11.0.

text.p: The Money Magazine/ABC News index of consumer comfort held steady at 11.0 in the week ended July 20 from the prior week.

In a separate question, of 515 adults polled for the two weeks ended July 20, 11 percent said they expected the budget bill being negotiated by Congress and President Clinton would result in lower their taxes. However, 39 percent believed it would raise their taxes, while 38 percent feel it won't affect their taxes at all.
The survey polls consumers nationwide about the national economy, personal finances and their willingness to spend.

Respondents' confidence in the economy held steady unchanged at 14. Confidence in personal finances fell to 24 from 26, while the rating of buying climate gained two points to -4 from -6 in the prior week.
Regionally, confidence fell in the West and Northeast, while holding steady in the Midwest, but attitudes rose in the South.
The current poll has a margin error of plus or minus 3.5 percentage points, while the separate question's error margin is plus or minus five points.
